messages:
Maya: Quick profiling update — after the kernel selector change last night, prefill vs decode split skewed much more toward decode. wondering if we regressed for p95 on short prompts. :thinking:
Alex: Can you paste the numbers? short prompts meaning <128 tokens?
Maya: yes <128. here's a quick flame summary from the heapprof run on canary (10k requests):
```
prefill_total_ms: 36
decode_total_ms: 142
kernel_prefill_ms: 12
kernel_decode_ms: 118
kv_lookup_ms: 8
batching_overhead_ms: 18
queue_wait_ms (microbatching): 26
```
Maya: p50 ~= 62ms, p95 ~= 210ms, p99 ~= 380ms for this slice. baseline before selector change was p95 ~140ms.
Ryan: Oof. So decode dominated and queue_wait is non-trivial. Did the kernel switch force a slower decode kernel for short sequences?
Maya: Looks like kernel heuristics chose the vectorized decode path that expects larger microbatches — it reduces per-token compute but increases scheduling jitter for small bursts.
Tessa: We enabled the new kernel-fallback policy that prefers lower-cost kernels when occupancy high. Might be choosing wrong for tiny batches.
Alex: Interesting — microbatch size distribution shows a spike at 1-4 then heavy tail to 12-16 when bursty. If selector assumes bimodal, it mispredicts.
Ryan: Two angles: (1) prevent the selector from switching to the vectorized decode kernel if mean_batch_size < 6, (2) preferentially warm KV cache for endpoints with many short prompts so we avoid decode extra hops.
Maya: Agreed. I also noticed KV cache misses add ~8ms per request on average during cold windows; warming reduces p99 more than p95.
Tessa: Any idea about batching_overhead_ms 18 — that's our enqueue/dequeue and RPC plumbing. Could we shave that by moving to a lighter scheduling loop for short-lived sessions?
Alex: There was a recent change to the microbatcher lock to optimize throughput — maybe it introduced extra spin time for small batches.
Maya: I profiled threads: spin wait increased by ~12ms in many runs around the switch.
Ryan: Proposed experiments: A) force microbatch_target=4 for a canary and compare p95/p99, B) add a kernel selector rule: if seq_len<128 && batch_mean<6 -> prefillsafe kernel, C) aggressive KV prefetch for the first request of a session.
Tessa: Also run a regression sweep for the last two kernel heuristics commits — tag the exact commit id in the canary job. infra-bot can we schedule?
infra-bot: deploybot: Canary job scheduled for cluster-gamma: run_id=canary-233999-c2, tests: p50/p95/p99, sample=12k, ramps=5m.
Alex: For the canary, include a trace-level flag so we can correlate kernel choice per request. add header X-Kernel-Choice to logs.
Maya: Will add. Also logging KV hit/miss per request (0/1) and microbatch size.
Ryan: If p99 stays high, fallback plan is to force fallback decode kernel at 99th percentile detection: detect rising tail and rollback kernel choice for 5m. Could be reactive but safer.
Tessa: Need to watch throughput regression if we force fallback — tradeoff expected. Add throughput numbers to the canary metrics.
Maya: Action items:
- Maya: instrument X-Kernel-Choice + KV hit logs in canary (ticket INF-4523)
- Alex: run microbatch_target=4 vs default in parallel canaries, collect p50/p95/p99 (ticket INF-4524)
- Ryan: prototype selector rule and bench kernels with seq_len buckets (ticket INF-4525)
- Tessa: run regression sweep on kernel heuristics commits and surface suspect CLs (ticket INF-4526)
- infra-bot: schedule canaries and attach artifacts to run_id=canary-233999-c2
Maya: Rough ETA: initial canary data in ~2 hours, will dump perf table here.
Alex: If canary shows p95 <= 160ms and p99 <= 250ms with microbatch_target=4, we can consider rolling the selector tweak.
Ryan: Also add a short A/B to test KV prefetch: prefetch-first-token vs no-prefetch — hypothesis: prefetch reduces p99 by ~30-50ms.
Tessa: FYI: we should update docs of kernel heuristics so oncall knows to look at microbatch histograms when debugging p95 regressions.
Maya: Thanks all — will post the canary summary when ready. :thumbsup:
